feature: A copy can be changed without leaving the family
summary: An original now chooses which of its parts are adjustable, and every copy can set those without breaking the link back. Detach turns a copy into ordinary layers when you want out.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, on a blank canvas. Flags are on by default; View ▸ Show Library if the shelf is not up.

try.do: Draw a filled box and type a text label over it, select both, press ⌘G.
Press ⌥⌘K and type a name for the component.
In the Component section, click Add and pick your label under Wording.
Drag the component's tile off the Library onto the canvas twice, to place two copies.
Select one copy and type different words into its knob.
Select the original, double click into its label and nudge it down with the arrow keys.
Select the copy you changed and click the revert arrow beside its knob.
Press ⌥⌘B on a copy to detach it.

evaluate: Is Add on the ORIGINAL the place you would look for making a part adjustable, or did you expect to select the part itself and expose it from there?
Does the Add menu, grouped by Wording / Show or hide / Choice, tell you what each knob will do before you pick one?
When you nudged the original, was it obvious that the copy you had changed kept its own wording and still followed everything else?
Is the revert arrow findable, and does it read as 'go back to the original' rather than 'undo'?
Detach says so in a pill because nothing on screen changes. Is that enough, or should the layers row look different too?
rough: Screen Recording was granted, so every shot here is the real window, taken by Scripts/playtest/component-override-walk.json and component-choice-walk.json.

A choice knob (screenshot 3, 2026-09-03-component-overrides-3-choice.png) needs a group of alternatives inside the component, which nothing in the app helps you build yet: you group two shapes by hand and then expose the group. The knob works, the path to it is unguided.

A wording knob is named after the words it exposes, so right after you add it the row reads 'Auto-enhance | Auto-enhance' until you either rename the knob or change the copy. Renaming is one field away in the original's list, but the duplication looks odd on first sight.

Changed from the mock: the Add menu is grouped by KIND with only the layers each knob suits, not every layer times every kind. Cut: the mock's 'Custom property…' row and its separate 'Instance props' section, since a copy's knobs belong in the copy's own Component section.
A long wording override still overflows the box it sits in. There is no auto layout, so this is a known limit rather than a bug.
A knob cannot reach into a copy nested inside the original, and knobs cannot be reordered.
Detach is one way: undo is the only path back, and there is no re-attach.
